Fetch data in the background as the signed-in user

Source: R/task.R
oauth_db_task.Rd

Create a task inside server() from an existing database helper or API client. Credentials stay coordinated by the owning Shiny session; each invocation opens its own connection or client in a mirai worker.

Usage

oauth_db_task(source, method = "query", min_valid_for = 120, compute = NULL)

Arguments

source

A database helper such as oauth_db_azure_postgres() (pass con, not con()), or a shinyOAuthDB API client.

method

Operation name. "query" uses DBI::dbGetQuery() for DBI connections and $query() for API clients. "execute" uses DBI::dbExecute() for DBI connections. Other names select native client methods, e.g. "select" or "search". A self-contained function defined at the top level may instead take the worker's connection/client as its first argument. Use namespace-qualified functions inside that function.

min_valid_for

Minimum token lifetime requested before dispatch, in seconds. Allow for queueing and the operation. Workers do not receive refresh tokens and cannot refresh a copied access token.

compute

Optional mirai compute-profile name. Use a separate profile for database work to reserve the default pool for OAuth operations.

Value

A task with $invoke(...), $result(), $status() and $cancel(). Invocation arguments go to the selected operation. Busy invocations are ignored and return FALSE; accepted invocations return TRUE, invisibly. result() waits quietly before completion, checks authorization on every read, and returns ordinary R data. Native handles cannot leave the worker. Status is "initial", "running", "success" or "error". Cancelled or invalidated results report "initial" until another invocation is accepted.

Details

mirai (2.5.1 or newer) is installed with shinyOAuthDB. Configure mirai::daemons() once before the server starts, and stop those workers when the app stops. The task never starts a worker pool itself. Enable async = TRUE on shinyOAuth's module separately for background OAuth operations.

Sign-out, account changes, permission loss and session end invalidate results and attempt to cancel pending worker work. Cancellation cannot undo a query or write already accepted by a server. Operations are never automatically replayed after a credential change. A worker's token snapshot expires after the requested lifetime budget; HTTP 401 does not refresh that snapshot or replay the operation. Choose sufficient lifetime for long polling/downloads.

API tasks reuse the backend's request, parameter, TLS and result-handling code. Fabric API tasks acquire all token groups configured on their source; configure targets for the services used by that task. Resolve reactive connection usernames in the owning session; pass query inputs to invoke().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Once at app startup:
mirai::daemons(2)
shiny::onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))

# Inside server(), with con created by a database helper:
rows <- oauth_db_task(con)
shiny::observeEvent(input$load, rows$invoke("SELECT current_user"))
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable(rows$result())

# An HTTP client uses the same pattern:
orders <- oauth_db_task(postgrest, method = "select")
shiny::observeEvent(input$load_orders, {
  orders$invoke("orders", order = "id.asc", limit = 20L)
})
output$orders <- shiny::renderTable(orders$result())
} # }
